Notification HubPartitioning guide

How notifications
move through
nine partitions.

notification-hub writes each day's notifications into one of nine partitions. At midnight it clears the slot for the new day, drops anything older than the retention window, and starts again. This guide covers the production environment only, showing the rules — and the state for any day.

A worked example, not live data.

Selected day at a glance

01The idea

A partition is a numbered slice of the table.

Notification tables can grow very large. Partitioning splits the rows into nine smaller pieces that share the same columns. The service chooses a piece by the day, so it can write a day's notifications into one slice and clear old slices without scanning everything.

The slices are called p0 to p8. They are not nine copies of the data: every notification row belongs to exactly one partition. A day's rows live together, which is what makes cleanup a single, predictable operation.

One notification table9 slices

02The cycle

One day forward, every day.

Days move through the slots in a fixed order: p0, p1, p2 … p8, then back to p0. The same slot comes around every nine days, so a day's data has a known home before it arrives.

For the technically curious: the slot is the number of calendar days since 1 January 2000, modulo 9. The formula is in the technical details.

03The cleanup

At 00:00, three things happen.

The rotation is a small, ordered routine. It runs every day in Europe/Paris, and the order matters: the new day's slot is cleared before anything is written to it.

01

Clear the incoming slot

The slot for the new day is truncated — emptied completely — before it is written. By the rotation's own rules it should already be empty; the clear is the final guarantee.

02

Drop what is past retention

Any slot whose day is older than the retention window is truncated. The service keeps 7 days + today.

03

Write the new day

The day's notifications go into its slot. The same partition number is used in all three notification tables.

Operational note: the cleanup is scheduled for 00:00 Paris. It runs hourly and retries at the next hour if it cannot get the lock; see Technical details.

04The rules

The retention window.

Retention is how many past days the service keeps, not counting today. The window decides how many of the nine slots hold data; the rest stay empty and wait for their turn.

Retention 7 days + today kept, plus today
Slots in use 8 / 9 of nine slots
  • Nine partitions, p0–p8, in a fixed order.
  • One day per midnight; the next day takes the next slot.
  • The incoming slot is truncated before it is written.
  • Anything older than retention is truncated.
  • Three tables share the partition number: notifications, status_history, payload.
  • The cleanup is scheduled for 00:00 and retries next hour if locked.

Retention is fixed in this guide at 7 days + today. If the service configuration changes, update the page constant and this section together.

05The schedule

The next nine midnights.

For the selected scenario, this is the full nine-day cycle. The first row is the next 00:00 after the selected day. The incoming day takes one slot; the oldest retained day falls out of the window and becomes empty.

00:00 onNew day usesSlot that ages out (day dropped)

Only one slot changes from in-use to empty per midnight. A slot that ages out is truncated again when it comes back around as the incoming slot, even though it is already empty.

06For engineers

Technical details

Technical details about the formula, retention, rotation and tables

Slot formula

slot = ((day − 2000-01-01) mod 9 + 9) mod 9. The day is a calendar day; date arithmetic is done on UTC date-only values, while “today” is resolved in Europe/Paris.

Retention

retention = 7. “In use” means today plus the 7 retention days, so 8 slots hold data and 1 is empty. Empty slots = 9 − live slots.

Rotation

At 00:00 Paris: truncate the incoming partition, truncate partitions older than retention, then write the new day. The job runs hourly; a lock failure retries at the next hour.

Tables

notifications (rows and primary metadata), status_history (SENT, PENDING, …), and payload (the notification payload) in the notification-hub database. The same partition number is used in all three, so truncating a partition clears the matching rows in each.

This page is a static model. It does not read from the database; the selected date is treated as the day being modelled. The date range is 2000-01-01 to 2100-12-31. Retention constants and the cleanup retry are documented here for maintenance.

Times are Europe/Paris. The first day of the model is 1 January 2000.
